verdict: Extra Space grew revenue 4% to $890M and squeezed more profit from the same stores by cutting their running costs, while a far smaller loss on property sales than a year ago made headline profit jump.

segments.name: Property rental
segments.note: Rent paid by people and businesses storing their things — up 3%.

segments.name: Tenant reinsurance
segments.note: Insurance tenants buy to cover what they store — up 4%.

segments.name: Management fees & other
segments.note: Fees for running storage sites owned by others, plus other income — up 7%.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The wearing-out cost of the storage properties — a non-cash charge.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — head office, finance, legal and HR.

opex.name: Tenant reinsurance costs
opex.note: Paying claims on the tenant insurance it sells.

opex.name: Loss on real estate sold
opex.note: Loss on properties sold or marked for sale — far below the $105M loss a year ago.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $151M plus $10M of non-cash interest, partly offset by $37M of interest income, $17M of earnings from joint ventures and a $14M joint-venture impairment loss, net.

takeaways.title: Same stores earned more
takeaways.text: Stores open in both years took in 2.7% more rent and spent 1.8% less to run, so their net operating income rose 4.6% to $505M. Occupancy ended the quarter at 94.0%.

takeaways.title: Cash profit per share rose
takeaways.text: Core FFO — funds from operations, the cash-profit measure landlords use because it adds back property depreciation — rose 4.3% to $2.17 per share, and the company raised its full-year guide to $8.40-$8.50.

takeaways.title: Buying back its own shares
takeaways.text: Extra Space repurchased 2.4 million of its own shares for $327M in the quarter and paid a $1.62-per-share dividend — returning cash instead of chasing growth.

oneTimers: A $6M loss on real estate assets held for sale and sold, versus a $105M loss in Q3 2025 — the main reason GAAP net income attributable to shareholders rose 49% to $248M.
A $14M impairment and loss on joint-venture interests, partly offset by $17M of earnings and dividend income from unconsolidated ventures.
footerNote: REIT format: revenue is rent, tenant insurance and management fees; direct costs are property operating costs. Amounts are rounded to the nearest $M from the release's thousands (total revenue $889.8M). Net income of $259M is the total before $12M allocated to non-controlling interests; $248M was attributable to common stockholders. FFO and Core FFO are non-GAAP measures the company reports alongside GAAP results.
